name: Tyson Foods Russellville Distribution Center - Russellville AR

citations.claim: Fully active food-industry campus at 4820 E Main St: two ~250m refrigerated buildings with long dock faces, ~200+ trailer drop yard, on-site feed mill and rail dock. Street View 2025-09 and 2026-02 both show the yard fully populated with trailers, i.e. current operation, not idled or vacant.

The query 'Tyson Foods Distribution Center, Russellville, AR' resolves ROOFTOP to 4820 E Main St, Russellville, AR 72802 (35.2604842, -93.0662256) - the exact CRM seed point and the center of this campus.
A trailer inside the fenced yard carries WRIGHT BRAND ('PIG OUT!') livery. Wright Brand is a Tyson Foods brand, corroborating Tyson operation of this yard.

verification.imageryDate: 2026 satellite; Street View 2026-02 (west approach), 2025-09 (E Main frontage), 2019-09 (entrance apron)
verification.rationale: Location is pinned with certainty (rooftop geocode of the CRM address lands dead-center on an active food campus) and imagery shows current, heavy operation; Tyson operatorship rests on Tier-3 corroboration only because the session web-search budget was exhausted, so the verdict is capped at probable. Divestiture/closure gauntlet run 2026-08-12: this site was checked by name against Tyson's announced closures 2023-2026 and does not appear on that list.

divestitureCitation.claim: Tyson closure sweep 2023-2026 checked this site by name against the announced-closure list (2023 poultry: Noel MO, Corydon IN, Glen Allen VA, Van Buren AR; 2024: Perry IA pork, North Little Rock AR; 2025: Emporia KS beef, 2x Original Philly PA prepared; 2026: Lexington NE beef closed Jan 20 2026, Rome GA prepared closing May 31 2026). This site does not appear on it. Checked against agriculturedive.com, kcur.org and wrdw.com reporting; swept 2026-08-12.

fieldNotes.site: Not a standalone warehouse. The CRM address 4820 E Main St resolves to a full Tyson complex on the south side of I-40 east of Russellville: two ~250 m long refrigerated production/distribution buildings, an on-site feed mill with grain bins and a bulk-loadout, a large fenced trailer drop yard, a rail-served dock, and a separate south-east support building. Audited as one campus.
fieldNotes.truckGate: FALSE with good evidence. The main truck approach off E Main St (US-64) at 35.2598,-93.0620 is a wide open concrete apron with a generous corner radius and no barrier arm, no sliding gate, no pinch-point (z20 satellite). Street View from 2019-09 sits ON that apron and the 2025-09 / 2026-02 panos run along the frontage and into the site - Google's car drove the internal road past the employee lot and feed mill, which is only possible on an uncontrolled entrance. The secondary north-west access off the west public road (35.2629,-93.0706, SV 2026-02) is likewise an open concrete drive with no gate and no fence across it.
fieldNotes.guardShack: FALSE. No booth at either entrance in z19/z20 satellite or in any Street View frame. The one small mid-yard structure at 35.25947,-93.06422 is a ~30 x 25 m flat-roof office with rooftop HVAC and a staff car park beside it - a driver/dispatch office in the middle of the drop yard, an order of magnitude too large for a gate booth and not positioned at any property entrance.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: FALSE by rule - there is no truck gate, so remote gate service does not apply. No kiosk or call box was visible at either entrance.
fieldNotes.perimeterFence: Chain-link fencing does run along the E Main frontage of the trailer drop yard (clearly visible in the 2019-09 and 2025-09 Street View frames). The fence is present but the vehicle openings in it are not controlled.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: From the E Main apron to the nearest dock face is roughly 500 m of internal road across open paved yard. Queue depth is effectively unlimited.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: FALSE. E Main St here is a rural two-lane with wide shoulders and the site has hundreds of metres of internal stacking before any dock. A gate queue could not reach the public road.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: TRUE for the primary E Main drive, which is a single two-way drive used both directions. Flagged rather than entryExitSeparate because the second (north-west) access serves the north side of the campus rather than acting as a dedicated out-gate. truckGateCount is set to 2 to record both openings.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: TRUE on physical room only. The E Main apron is roughly 40 m of unused paved width and the internal road is far wider than a single lane, so an express/bypass lane could be added trivially. Since there is no gate today this is greenfield room, not a bypass around an existing checkpoint.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: 50+, estimated at ~85 total and flagged as approximate. Building A's west face carries a continuous row of ~40 backed-in trailers over a ~245 m dock wall (z19 count of 23-24 trailers over a 141 m stretch). Building B's east face carries a further ~30-35 positions over ~190 m. Add the rail dock canopy on the south end and short faces. Individual door leaves are under canopies and are not directly countable from overhead.
fieldNotes.dropArea: 50+. The fenced trailer lot east of the buildings runs roughly 220 x 150 m and holds tightly packed rows of dropped trailers (z19 shows trailers parked shoulder to shoulder at roughly 3 m centres). Visible count across the whole site is on the order of 230; capacity around 300. Both numbers are +/- 20% reads off overhead imagery, not exact counts.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: TRUE on physical evidence, inferred on function. Two entirely separate dock banks exist on different buildings and different faces - building A's west face and building B's east face - plus a rail dock on the south end. Which bank is inbound versus outbound cannot be determined from imagery.
fieldNotes.scale: FALSE, but listed as uncertain. No unambiguous scale deck or scale house was resolvable at z20 anywhere on the truck path, including around the feed mill where bulk feed trailers load. A feed mill of this size would normally have a truck scale, so absence here is a limit of the imagery rather than a confident negative.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: TRUE. Two large production/distribution buildings, a feed mill with grain bins and elevator tower, a mid-yard driver office, a south-east support building with its own dock and car park, and a rail-served covered dock.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE, directly evidenced. A spur leaves the mainline on the south boundary and runs into the property alongside a covered rail dock on the south end of building B; hopper cars are parked on it in the 2026 imagery (z19 at 35.25892,-93.06617).
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Rural. Edge of Russellville (population under 30k), farmland and woodland on three sides, an interstate on the fourth. Small-town industrial, so Rural per the rubric.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: FALSE. Directly alongside I-40 with a town two miles west; cellular coverage is very unlikely to be the constraint.
fieldNotes.confidence: Capped at medium. The physical read is strong (2026 satellite, three Street View vintages, multiple zoom levels) but Tyson operatorship rests on Tier-3 corroboration only, since the session web-search budget was exhausted before the Tier-1 locator / careers / 10-K checks could be run.
